title: Biased-Noise Quantum Reed-Solomon Codes and a Tornado Concatenation for Cat Qubits
summary: Dissipative cat qubits exponentially suppress one Pauli error channel with the mean photon number, leaving the conjugate bit-flip error as the dominant failure mode. This strong noise bias makes the full machinery of general quantum error correction unnecessary: a code need only protect against a single error type, and any classical linear code can be promoted to a Clifford stabilizer code that does exactly this. We use this observation to build a bit-flip-only quantum Reed-Solomon (RS) code. Starting from the maximum-distance-separable RS code [7, 3, 5] over GF($2^3$), we binary-expand it…
